scope.selectionMethod: Fifty still-held rows with recurrent historical owner evidence; all checked against current exact source and owner record. Some historical leads are rejected despite lexical overlap.

screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: One kind gesture created a ripple in water across the team.
screenedRows.sourceMeaning: An effect spreading from a small starting point; a water image.
screenedRows.currentDecisionReason: Source a ripple in water does not fit canonical 1692’s like a ripple in water simile or target pattern. Hold for idiomaticity and possible ripple effect wording review.
screenedRows.ownerMeaning: Spreading from a small beginning to affect others, through an explicit water-wave comparison.
screenedRows.ownerGrammar: an action/feeling spreads like a ripple in water; like marks the comparison; specify what spreads and the observed response
screenedRows.rationaleAndNextGate: Source omits the simile marker like and its water/team imagery is awkward; not the owner’s exact comparison.

screenedRows.expression: all fireworks and not much substance
screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: The speech was all fireworks and not much substance.
screenedRows.sourceMeaning: Exciting in appearance but shallow in content; fireworks is a figurative spectacle.
screenedRows.currentDecisionReason: All fireworks and not much substance is a creative spectacle-versus-content blend; verify whether a standard reusable contrast exists. Provisional editorial decision; independent review remains open.
screenedRows.ownerMeaning: Impressive presentation or publicity outweighs genuine practical value.
screenedRows.ownerGrammar: More show than substance; compare visible display with what the event or proposal actually delivers. All glitter and no substance is a related display-versus-value judgement; glitter refers to surface attraction, not literal decorative material.
screenedRows.ownerTargetPattern: \bmore show than substance\b|\ball glitter and no substance\b
screenedRows.rationaleAndNextGate: Same broad appearance/substance theme, but fireworks is a different figurative target from show or glitter.

screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: A simple line can land a punch in the final verse.
screenedRows.sourceMeaning: Have a strong impact; a fixed boxing metaphor.
screenedRows.currentDecisionReason: The exact source line A simple line can land a punch in the final verse may be a strained lyric-line collocation relative to pack a punch; verify idiomaticity and target-unit choice before teaching it.
screenedRows.ownerMeaning: Be received, understood or have an intended communicative effect; much better adds a stronger positive comparison with another version or occasion.
screenedRows.ownerGrammar: a message, joke, explanation or lesson lands with an audience; landed for past reference. Lands much better compares reception or impact. A lesson lands can emphasise understanding or becoming meaningful through examples, not necessarily being liked.
screenedRows.rationaleAndNextGate: Owner highlights bare land; source targets land a punch, a stronger boxing idiom with a distinct force boundary.

screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: Community performances help keep their roots alive.
screenedRows.sourceMeaning: Maintain a connection with cultural origins; a plant metaphor.
screenedRows.currentDecisionReason: Same-sense later owner 4470 was reviewed, but the alias contract requires an earlier canonical source ordinal. Retain this hold until ownership can be resolved without changing existing IDs.
screenedRows.ownerMeaning: Stay connected to origins or defining traditions over time, including while changing or growing.
screenedRows.ownerGrammar: Keep + possessive + roots, optionally followed by alive; roots is figurative. Name the actual origin, practice or people preserved. A new format can make the contrast visible, but change is not required for keeping roots alive.
screenedRows.rationaleAndNextGate: Exact full-source detector match and same cultural-origin sense. The current decision explicitly blocks a direct alias because owner4470 was created from a later source; resolve the source-order/ID contract before any edit.

screenedRows.expression: the lesson can lose its teeth
screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: Without follow-through, the lesson can lose its teeth.
screenedRows.sourceMeaning: A consequence becomes too weak to matter; a teeth metaphor.
screenedRows.currentDecisionReason: A lesson losing its teeth adapts an enforcement metaphor to a consequence; this application needs editorial review. Provisional editorial decision; independent review remains open.
screenedRows.ownerMeaning: The law has effective enforcement powers or penalties, not just words on paper.
screenedRows.ownerGrammar: the law has real teeth; teeth is a fixed plural metaphor for practical power.
screenedRows.rationaleAndNextGate: Weakening a lesson’s consequence differs from the law’s enforceable penalty sense.

screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: Parents cannot always hold their hand on the journey to school.
screenedRows.sourceMeaning: Guide someone closely; a fixed hand idiom.
screenedRows.currentDecisionReason: Hold: hold their hand repeats the figurative guidance sense of provisional 3611, now held pending comparison with existing canonical 1586 and detector coverage. Resolve owner before assigning this repeat.
screenedRows.ownerMeaning: Offer reassuring companionship or close guidance through a difficult experience; a negative form can stress that this constant help will not always be available.
screenedRows.ownerGrammar: hold someone’s hand through a difficulty; hold your hand every step of the way stresses constant guidance, often negated to encourage independent action. This is figurative when no actual hand is being held.
screenedRows.ownerTargetPattern: (?:\bfriends\s+can\s+hold\s+your\s+hand\b)|(?:\b(?:hold|holds|held|holding) your hand every step of the way\b)
screenedRows.rationaleAndNextGate: Journey to school can involve literal parental hand-holding; owner teaches sustained figurative reassurance.

screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: During a dull lecture, the mind can switch off.
screenedRows.sourceMeaning: Stop paying attention or thinking actively; a figurative phrasal verb.

screenedRows.ownerMeaning: Stop paying attention or engaging almost immediately.
screenedRows.ownerGrammar: listeners / students switch off straight away when + reason
screenedRows.rationaleAndNextGate: Dull-lecture switch off is general attention lapse, while owner has immediate disengagement; selected 4257 now teaches gradual drift.

screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: Your carefully planned day can fall apart when constant alerts scatter it.
screenedRows.sourceMeaning: Break focus into unrelated pieces; a physical verb describes attention figuratively.
screenedRows.currentDecisionReason: Scatter it has an unclear pronoun and seems tied to a one-off image, not a stable reusable target.
screenedRows.ownerMeaning: Become so upset that it is difficult to think calmly or deal with the immediate situation.
screenedRows.ownerGrammar: a person falls/fell/is falling apart; intransitive, without an object. The supplied over every small setback adds a particular trigger and frequency, not part of the fixed verb. Distinguish objects breaking and a system failing. Fall to pieces uses the same intransitive emotional construction in context; inflect fall, leaving to pieces fixed.
screenedRows.rationaleAndNextGate: Source targets scatter it; owner fall apart matches incidental words but teaches a person becoming upset.

screenedRows.rationaleAndNextGate: Lean into a local character plausibly shares active-embrace sense with lean into healthy habits, but the owner currently limits the object to wellbeing routines. Test whether a broader quality/strategy target keeps one learner decision.

screenedRows.rationaleAndNextGate: At once in multiple lights going out can mean simultaneously or immediately; the source does not disambiguate owner3142’s after-trigger timing.
